title: エネルギー固体化学
subtitle: Solid State Chemistry for Energy Conversion and Storage
keywords: Chemical substances 2.Crystal structures 3.Electrical properties of solids 4.Band structures 5.Magnetic properties of solids
educationalGoal: Three general objectives will be addressed in this course: -Learn about methods to form and analyze solids for energy conversion and storage. -Acquire the ability to solve problems using the appropriate analysis method. -Acquire the ability to synthesize and analyze inorganic compounds to fabricate optical, electrical, and magnetic devices.
advice: There will be two one-hour examinations during the term and a regularly scheduled final examination. The exercise sheets will be also distributed in the class. All of the exams will be closed-notes and closed-book, although the key equations will be provided on the exam sheets.
books: Textbooks: Peter Atkins and Julio De Paula, Elements of Physical Chemistry, 7th Ed., Oxford University Press Reference books: Reserved books: Peter Atkins, Julio De Paula, James Keeler, Physical Chemistry (11th Edition), Oxford University Press; Levine, Ira N., Quantum Chemistry (7th Edition) Pearson; Anthony R. West, Solid State Chemistry and its Applications (2nd Edition) Student Edition, Wiley
requiredKnowledge: Student should be familiar with: 1. Fundamentals of physics and mathematics. 2. Fundamentals of 1st and 2nd year university chemistry.

achievementLevels.ideal: -Describe the crystal structures of solids and apply that knowledge to solve problems. -Describe the use of diffractometry to analyze the crystal structure of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems. -Describe analytical methods used for determining the elemental composition of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems. -Describe the electronic band structure of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems. -Describe the principles and functions of optical and electronic devices.
achievementLevels.standard: -Describe the crystal structures of solids. -Describe the use of diffractometry to analyze the crystal structure of solids. -Describe analytical methods used to determine the elemental composition of a solid. -Describe the electronic band structure of solids. -Describe the principles and functions of optical and electronic devices. -Describe applications of solids to solar cells and fuel cells.
